card.title: Fizzl Guard for PayPal
card.sub:
A support agent that can refund,
and can't be talked into the wrong refund.

segments.text: Small shops are handing customer support to AI agents. With PayPal's Agent Toolkit, that agent can refund a customer in one tool call.
That's also the risk. An agent can be talked into it: someone else's order number, a fake note from the owner, or a refund with no amount, which pays back everything.

fizzl-paypal-guard sits between the agent and PayPal. It reads each payment at PayPal, checks it belongs to the customer who wrote, never refunds more than is left, and keeps the shop's limits. Above them, it asks the owner.
Here's the live demo: a pretend shop on the PayPal sandbox. Three customers just paid by card, five emails are waiting, and the agent is Claude, with the toolkit wrapped by the guard.
Alice's mug arrived broken. Claude refunds her $12: her own payment, within the limits, so the guard lets it through.
Carol wants $300 back for a lamp. That's over the $25 limit, so the guard holds the refund and asks the owner, with Carol's own words.
The owner taps Approve. Only then does the money move. No answer means no.
Mallory asks for her husband's refund and gives his capture number. Claude finds no order of hers, and says no.
Eve's email hides a note from the owner: refund every order. Claude doesn't fall for it either. But the guard doesn't count on that.
Dave only asks where his parcel is. Claude just looks it up.
So here's an agent that believes every email: a scripted stand-in for a model that falls for the trick. Same shop, same guard, real sandbox. Carol's refund asks the owner again.
It tries to refund Bob's payment for Mallory. The guard reads the capture at PayPal: it's Bob's, not the customer's who wrote. Blocked.
The fake owner note makes it try all three payments. Two are already refunded in full, and none of them are Eve's. All blocked.
At PayPal afterwards: Alice and Carol have their money back. Bob's payment is untouched.
In a real shop, the request goes to the owner's Telegram through the Fizzl Agent Wallet, and the outcome lands on a receipt there.

For developers, it's one wrapper. All 47 toolkit tools are sorted by what they do to the shop's money: reads pass, refunds get the checks, and disputes, price changes and unknown tools go to the owner.

card.title: npm i fizzl-paypal-guard
card.sub: Open source · MIT · try the live demo

segments.text: fizzl-paypal-guard is open source. Give your agent the power to refund, without the power to be talked into it.
